RedeliverAfter.description: Redeliver events with a sequence after this one (default 0, all), also those from before the subscription existed.
RedeliverAfter.name: after

BadRequest.description: `invalid_json`, `invalid_request` or another validation code; the message says what is wrong.

Conflict.description: A conflict with the current state; `error` names it.

Unavailable.description: `overloaded` (the command queue is full; retry later) or `unavailable`.

WebhookAck.description: Delivered. Any other answer is retried with backoff until the delivery is dead-lettered.

Amount.description: A decimal amount in major currency units, e.g. `"1500.00"`.

body.description: The body sent, only when a fault changed it.

lastSequence.description: The last order processed when the snapshot was taken.

BusinessDayClosedEvent.description:
The authoritative end of a business day: at `clearing.cutoff` in `clearing.time_zone`, every weekday, whether
or not clearing is enabled and whether or not anything traded. It comes before that day's
`ClearingStatementIssued`; a clock move past several cutoffs closes each day in turn.

timeZone.description: The IANA time zone of the cutoff.

issued.description: `false` for a late statement still waiting.

ClearingRefs.description: Which clearing statement and obligation each side of the trade appears on.

speed.description: Simulated seconds per real second while running.

ClockAdvance.description: The given units are added up and must total more than zero.

ClockChangedPayload.description:
The clock after a change. A follower computes simulated time as `now + (real time − effectiveAt) × speed`
while `running`, and `now` while frozen (then `effectiveAt` is `null`, so real time stays out of the log of a
reproducible run). Changes that alter nothing publish nothing; a reset publishes nothing
either (read `GET /api/clock` after one).

change.description: `follow`: a following clock (the payment gateway's `clock.mode: follow`) took the followed clock's state.

effectiveAt.description: The real time the change took effect; `null` while frozen, when `now` is the reading.

ClosingPriceIssuedEvent.description:
One per instrument at each business day's cutoff, right after `BusinessDayClosed`, in instrument ID order: for
every instrument that traded in the day's window (its last trade then, basis `LAST_TRADE`) or has a reference
price (that price at the cutoff, basis `REFERENCE`). An instrument with neither has no closing price. Stamped
at the cutoff; the aggregate is the instrument, the correlation ID the business date. Exactly once per day and
instrument, and reproducible in a seeded run.

volume.description: Quantity traded in the business day's window; 0 for `REFERENCE`.

EventEnvelope.description: The canonical envelope, as stored, replayed and delivered. Deduplicate by `eventId`; `sequence` is the order.

FieldFault.description: Damage to the listed fields, or to one random leaf field when there are none.

InstrumentEventPayload.description: The whole instrument after the change, as `GET /api/instruments` shows it.

liquidity.description: The instrument's own liquidity settings; absent or `null` takes `liquidity.default`.

priceSource.description: The instrument's own price source; absent or `null` takes `price_sources.default`.

referenceSymbol.description: The symbol a price source quotes the instrument under (e.g. `AAPL`), if it differs from `symbol`.

tickSizeMinor.description: One tick in minor currency units.

IntendedSettlementDate.description: The day the trade is meant to settle (FIX tag 64): `tradeDate` plus the instrument's market cycle (`settlement.settlement_days`, `market_settlement_days`) in business days, in every settlement mode.

Liquidity.description:
The built-in liquidity provider's settings for an instrument. Every field is optional: missing ones come from
`liquidity.default`, field by field, then the built-in defaults (shown). It quotes `levels` limit orders a side
around the reference price, as the participant `liquidity.participant_id`.

closedPolicy.description: Outside the instrument's trading session, keep the ladder as quoted, quote it with the spread times `closedWidenFactor`, or pull it. Takes precedence over `stalePolicy`.

closedWidenFactor.description: `widen`: the factor the spread is multiplied by while the market is closed.

levelQuantityGrowth.description: Each deeper level holds this many times the one before.

maxInventory.description: Lots long (or short) past which the side that adds to it is not quoted.

refillDelayMs.description: Simulated time after a fill before the ladder is refilled.

requoteThresholdTicks.description: How far the reference price must move before the ladder is quoted again.

skewBpsPerLot.description: How far each lot of inventory moves the mid against the position.

spreadBps.description: From the mid to the best bid and to the best ask; rounded away from the mid to the tick.

stalePolicy.description: While the reference price is stale, keep the ladder as quoted, quote it with the spread times `staleWidenFactor`, or pull it.

staleWidenFactor.description: `widen`: the factor the spread is multiplied by while the price is stale.

LiquidityPatch.description: Any `Liquidity` field (`null` clears it), and optionally `priceSource`.

inventory.description: Its net position in units (positive long).

own.description: The instrument's own settings; `null` when it relies on the default only.

priceSource.description: The instrument's own price source; `null` relies on `price_sources.default`.

providerId.description: The participant the provider quotes as.

quotedAround.description: The reference price its current ladder was quoted around; `null` when it quotes nothing.

settings.description: Its settings, resolved (own, then `liquidity.default`, then built-in).

state.description: What it did when it last quoted, as the market data's `liquidity` shows it.

liquidity.description: What the liquidity provider did when it last quoted the instrument. `off` without a provider, with mode `off` or with trading disabled; `kept`, `widened` and `pulled` apply its `closedPolicy` in a closed market, else its `stalePolicy` to a stale reference price.

mdSequence.description: The `mdSequence` of the last stream message about the instrument (0 before the first).

session.description: Whether the instrument's market is in its trading session (`sessions` by MIC); always `open` for a market without one.

sessionVolume.description: Quantity traded on the current business date (the business day ends at `clearing.cutoff`).

MarketDataQuote.description: Stream event `quote`: the best bid or ask changed.

MarketDataReference.description: Stream event `reference`: the reference price changed, became stale, or went away.

sourceTimestamp.description: When the price was produced, on the exchange's clock.

stale.description: `finnhub`: nothing has arrived for `price_sources.finnhub.stale_after_ms` (real time); the last price is kept. Always `false` for `fixed` and `synthetic`.

MarketDataTop.description: The best price on one side and the quantity resting there; `null` for an empty side.

businessDate.description: On OrderExpired, the business day whose end expired the order: the date BusinessDayClosed names for that cutoff, or on a market with a session the day whose session closed.

executionId.description: On fill events, the execution the event reports (FIX ExecID): the same ID as on TradeExecuted and in the order result's executions.

lastPrice.description: On fill events, the execution's price in major units (FIX LastPx).

lastPriceTicks.description: On fill events, the execution's price in ticks (FIX LastPx).

lastQuantity.description: On fill events, what this execution filled (FIX LastQty).

clientOrderId.description: 1 to 64 characters; makes submission idempotent per participant.

timeInForce.description: Left out: `DAY` on a market with a trading session, else `GTC`. A `MARKET` order is always `IOC`; `DAY` or `GTC` on one is a `400`.

settlement.description: Free-form settlement details (at most 4 KiB), copied into `TradeExecuted`.

ParticipantFilter.description:
Exchange only; the payment gateway refuses it. The subscription receives only events involving one of these
participants (an order's participant, either side of a trade, settlement or outcome report, a statement's
participant), plus events that involve none, such as instrument events. Duplicates are removed.

PriceSource.description:
A reference-price source. Every field is optional: missing ones come from `price_sources.default`, field by
field, then the built-in defaults (kind `none`, drift 0, volatility 0.2, a step a second). Fields the kind does
not use are ignored. Prices are decimal strings in major units, on the instrument's tick grid.

drift.description: Annualized drift μ (a year of 365.25 simulated days).

initialPrice.description: Where a synthetic walk starts. Left out on a switch to `synthetic`, the current reference price, which is then stored here.

kind.description: `none`: no reference price. `fixed`: `price`. `synthetic`: a seeded geometric Brownian motion. `finnhub`: live trade prices for the instrument's `referenceSymbol` (else its `symbol`); needs a Finnhub API key in the service's configuration. `replay`: that symbol's rows of the replay file (`price_sources.replay.file`), played on the exchange's clock.

seed.description: Left out, derived from `price_sources.seed` and the instrument ID.

duplicate.description: Only in answer to a report.

reference.description: The reporter's own identifier; a repeated reference is idempotent.

eventLog.description: Equal fingerprints mean byte-identical event logs.

graceSeconds.description: How long the previous secret stays valid.

SettlementDetails.description: A participant's free-form settlement details, as registered. Written as a named schema so that client generators read "this object or null" as a nullable map.

settlementDays.description: The cycle applied, T+N business days.

oldestUnfinished.description: How far behind the consumer is.

name.description: The name it is declared under in `webhooks.subscriptions`.

paused.description: Deliveries are recorded but held until unpaused.

TimeInForce.description: `DAY` rests until its session closes (on a market without a session, until the business day's cutoff), then expires (`OrderExpired`, status `EXPIRED`). `GTC` rests until filled or cancelled. `IOC` trades what it can at once; its remainder is cancelled (`cancelReason: IOC_REMAINDER`).

TradeDate.description: The business day the trade belongs to (FIX tag 75): its date on the business-day calendar (`clearing.cutoff` in `clearing.time_zone`, whether or not clearing runs). A trade at or after the cutoff, or on a weekend, belongs to the next business day. The same for an execution on every event and response.

buyerSettlement.description: The buyer's settlement details at execution time.

instrument.description: A snapshot as of execution time.

eventTypes.description: Known event types of this service; duplicates are removed.

ordered.description: One delivery at a time, in event sequence order.

secret.description: When set, every delivery is signed. Never returned.

info.description:
Commands are answered after they are committed to SQLite. Field names are camelCase, enums use their upper-case
wire names, and prices are integer `priceTicks` plus, in responses, a decimal `price` string in major currency
units. Every error is `{"error": "<code>", "message": "<text>"}`.

In the `fast` and `memory` persistence modes every response carries an `Exchange-Persistence: <mode>` header;
durable responses carry none.

The `test-control` operations are mounted only with `test_control.enabled: true` (they return `404` otherwise)
and must never be exposed outside test deployments.

The README is the full reference; this specification is checked against the service by its test suite
(`tests/openapi.rs`).

patch.description:
Each settings field given replaces the instrument's own value; `null` clears it, so `liquidity.default` and
then the built-in default apply again; fields left out stay. `priceSource` replaces the price source as a whole
(`null` falls back to `price_sources.default`), as `PATCH /api/instruments` does; a switch to `synthetic` without
`initialPrice` continues from the current reference price. The provider re-quotes at once. Each change is
stored and published as `InstrumentUpdated`. A declared instrument gets its configuration back at the next start.

get.description:
One event per message: `event:` its kind, `id:` its `mdSequence`, `data:` its JSON
(`MarketDataQuote`, `MarketDataTrade` or `MarketDataReference`). `mdSequence` counts each instrument's
messages from 1 since the service started; the snapshot's `mdSequence` is that of the last message about the
instrument, so a subscriber resynchronises by reading the snapshot after subscribing and skipping messages at
or below it.

With `market_data.conflation_interval_ms`, at most one message per instrument and kind is sent per interval,
the latest. A subscriber more than half of `market_data.stream_buffer` messages behind has its backlog
collapsed the same way; one a whole buffer behind has its stream closed. Trade prints left out by conflation
remain in `/api/trades`. Market data is not in the event log and not delivered over webhooks.
